output.brief: The evidence points mainly to Callerby's own decision, not Halden, as the cause of the slip. The tower crane and frame crew went to the Kestrel warehouse in October 2025, and the crane stayed away until April. The architect's register shows CO-09 was issued on 6 November, after the crane had already left. The other change orders were small interior layout changes. The platform's tamper-proof timestamps show the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The 41 "late" requests in the draft claim were mostly sitting in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before submission. The architect also answered the CO-09 structural query in four days. So do not submit the claim as drafted. It rests on a measure that overstates the architect's delay, and it would likely fail and damage credibility. The claim consultant's fee also depends on recovery, so their analysis should not be relied on. CO-09 may justify a small, properly evidenced extension, so have someone independent assess only that. Do not discipline the superintendent. He told the truth when asked, and a warning would discourage honesty. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet. Nothing shows it drove the crane move. Still unknown: why the crane moved, and the steel delivery picture. I'm fairly sure about the claim's weakness, less sure about the full split of causes.
